_comment: Configuration for tools/doc-currency/check.js. Sibling-JSON convention borrowed from tools/gas-lint/ (project-map.json, scope-map.json). Every exclusion here is load-bearing: see the comment above the check that reads it for why removing one makes the tool report correct documentation as wrong.
_comment_excludeDocs: Dated records, wholesale. Naming a function that was deleted is exactly what these exist to do — Round 14's CHANGELOG entry records that triggerCouncilSimulation() was removed, and flagging it would be flagging the record for being a record. LEADERHUB_WIP.md is here for the same reason: its body is per-session log entries, and 'Session 11 — added resolveTask()' stays true after resolveTask() is removed. Matched on basename, so cas-ccps/HISTORY.md and kos-personal/CHANGELOG.md are both covered.
_comment_supersededMarkers: A file-level banner speaks for the whole document, so a hit in the first bannerScanLines lines skips the file. This repo already uses these heavily and correctly — LEADERHUB_README.md's third line says callAI() 'neither exists in the code anymore', which is precisely the finding the tool would otherwise report against it twenty times.
_comment_externalSurfaceDocs: Docs describing Apps Script that lives in the operator's Script editor and was never committed here, mapped to the specific out-of-repo function names each one documents. PER-NAME ON PURPOSE: this was a flat array of paths, which marked a whole file unverifiable, and that is how LH_02_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md's "all AI calls go through callAI()" hid as a soft warning -- callAI was deleted from leader-hub's own HTML (see its "Removed: Gemini AI infrastructure" line), so it was never external at all. A name NOT on its doc's list is checked normally and errors if missing. Do not add a name here to silence a finding; only add one that genuinely lives in the uncommitted project. Committing those scripts would let an entry graduate off this list entirely.
_comment_historicalMarkers: Prose that marks a function reference as describing the past rather than instructing the reader. Checked against the enclosing blank-line-delimited paragraph. A fixed line window was tried first and was too loose: 'doesn't exist' is ordinary English before it is a marker, and USER_GUIDE.md's 'The deploy function only creates what doesn't exist' silently suppressed a real finding three lines away.
_comment_allowlistedNames: Names that read as this repo's own functions but aren't: platform APIs, other products' functions, and shell/tooling commands that happen to appear backticked with parens.
_comment_keyRegistryDocs: Docs that claim to be a complete registry of sheet columns or PropertiesService keys. Only these are checked for dead keys — a key mentioned in passing in a narrative doc is not a completeness claim.
_comment_acknowledgedMarkers: A registry row that admits its own status is documenting correctly, not drifting. Without this the tool's first output is a complaint about the three rows that were just labelled honestly.
_comment_allowlistedKeys: ALL-CAPS tokens in the registry docs that are not keys: value enums, column headers, folder names, and status strings.
